confirmation_bias: 🧠 Confirmation Bias Alert: Your recent reading heavily favors one perspective. Diversifying your sources builds a more complete understanding of the world.
🌀 Echo Chamber Warning: 80%+ of your content comes from a single ideological bubble. Try a 'perspective flip' with a source from the opposite side.
conspiracy_exposure: 🕵️ You've engaged with content from sources known for conspiracy theories. Here's a fact-checked analysis from a neutral outlet to provide context.
🧩 Critical Thinking Nudge: This topic has a history of misinformation. Cross-reference claims with multiple high-reliability sources before forming a conclusion.
satirical_exposure: 🎭 Satire Detected: This content is from a known satirical source. It's meant to be humorous, not factual. Enjoy responsibly!
low_diversity: 🧭 Your information diet is a bit narrow. Explore a new, highly-rated source today to broaden your horizons.
📈 Diversity Score Low: Challenge yourself! Read an article from a source you normally wouldn't.
balanced: ✅ Great job! Your information diet is well-balanced. Keep seeking diverse perspectives!
🌟 You're a critical consumer of news. Maintain this healthy skepticism and curiosity.

emotional.explanation: Designed to provoke anger and bypass critical thinking.
Creates artificial shock value to grab attention.
Pressures you to act without thinking.
Often used for non-critical news to grab attention.
Uses apocalyptic language to create panic.

fallacy.name: Straw Man
fallacy.pattern: \b(either you support|so you're saying|if you believe in|that means you think)\b
fallacy.explanation: Misrepresents an opponent's argument to make it easier to attack.

fallacy.name: Ad Hominem
fallacy.explanation: Attacks the person instead of the argument.

fallacy.name: False Dichotomy
fallacy.pattern: \b(either.*?or|you're either with us|only two choices|no middle ground)\b
fallacy.explanation: Presents only two options when more exist.

fallacy.name: Appeal to Emotion
fallacy.pattern: \b(imagine if|think of the children|how would you feel)\b
fallacy.explanation: Uses emotion to persuade rather than logic.

fallacy.name: Slippery Slope
fallacy.pattern: \b(if we allow|this will lead to|next thing you know)\b
fallacy.explanation: Suggests that a small first step leads to a chain of related events culminating in a significant impact.

deceptive.explanation: Vague authority, no specific experts named.
No link to actual study provided.
Anonymous sources - impossible to verify credibility.
